description: The National Satellite Meteorological Centre of the China Meteorological Administration also serves as China's National Space Weather Monitoring and Warning Centre. Its home page read on 2026-09-28 carries a three-day space weather forecast (that day: low solar activity with a low chance of M-class flares, geomagnetic activity quiet to unsettled, a quiet ionosphere), sections on satellite operations, cloud imagery, remote sensing applications, space weather and data sharing, a list of the ten Fengyun satellites in orbit out of 23 launched (FY-4C, FY-4B, FY-4A, FY-3H, FY-3F, FY-3G, FY-3E, FY-3D, FY-2H and FY-2G), the SWAP platform for real-time Fengyun-2 and Fengyun-4 data, and an emergency mechanism through which international users facing disasters can request Fengyun support. Coverage is global for satellite data and forecasts, from a Chinese national centre. Access is free to view; data sharing terms and registration were not read. Caveats: the space weather section and its indices were not opened past the home page summary, and English pages may lag the Chinese ones. It supports space weather warnings for power grids, GNSS and satellite operators. Related record: data-may-2024-storm-gic-observations holds storm impact measurements that complement the forecasts.
